topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition via PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns and germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptors and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the characteristics, cellular localization, and downstream intracellular signaling cascades of Toll-like receptors.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic PRRs and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe intracellular pattern recognition receptor families and the assembly of the inflammasome complex for processing pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the cellular processes of the acute inflammatory response, from sentinel cell activation and leukocyte extravasation to lymphatic drainage and systemic inflammatory complications.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is actively and passively terminated, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how persistent inflammation leads to chronic disease or containment.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and introduces the topic of the next lecture.
